newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania's Landsbergis to run for president.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania's Landsbergis to run for president.

text.p: Lithuanian independence hero Vytautas Landsbergis, hoping to seal a political comeback launched last year, said on Saturday he would run for president of the Baltic state.
"I will stand as a candidate in the next presidential election," Landsbergis told Reuters ahead of a conference of his Homeland Union Party, which is expected to name him as the party's candidate.
Lithuania's Landsbergis to run for president
The country is expected to hold a presidential election in December.

Landsbergis, a 64-year-old former music professor, led his country's independence struggle against Moscow. He stormed back into power when his Homeland Union Party unseated the governing former communists in parliamentary polls last year.

That victory was sweet revenge for Landsbergis, who had suffered a humiliating defeat at the hands of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDDP), the former communists, in 1992, just one year after his nation regained its independence.

Landsbergis, currently chairman of the country's parliament, will likely face his arch-political rival, President Algirdas Brazasukas, the former head of the country's Communist Party, in the election.
